correctness.rationale: Identical simultaneous zero insertions correspond to nonnegative increments on cyclic edge lengths. Translation of two-point supports is equivalent to matching one of two oriented arc lengths, and positivity proves exact oriented costs including the nested-arc infeasibility case. Sharing one endpoint gives absolute circular-distance sum minus n; disjoint endpoints give a cost at most n-4 via the four positive interpoint gaps. This proves the exact instance-wise formula, optimum one-gap realization, sharp \(n-3\) maximum, and \(4n\) extremizer count for every n>=4; n=2,3 covered separately. Independent exhaustive allocations for all 1595 ordered pairs through n=8 and 93992 formula/construction tests through n=18 passed; finite checks are expressly corroborative.

originality.rationale: The full-text 2026 source proves existence iff equal Hamming weight and a polynomial length bound, but explicitly lists exact shortest-padding length as an open issue. The present theorem supplies an instance-wise optimum, one-gap realization, worst-case formula and complete worst-pair count for the entire weight-two stratum. The older unrestricted-insertion criteria do not imply this zero-only length optimum. Actual published-index and literature variant searches produced no stronger covering result; absence from indexing is not uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The main paper expressly asks for optimal 0-padding lengths. This closes the first nontrivial sparse-weight stratum in an infinite parameter range, yielding exact per-instance costs and a single-gap construction, a sharp linear worst-case bound, and a structural classification/count of all worst ordered pairs. These are not routine substitutions into qualitative existence or the polynomial-length construction, and give a reusable boundary model for sparse inputs.
